text: Vocabulary is a constant source of worry and challenge. There has not been a one- stop solution for it yet. To solve this, the entire booklet has been created keeping in mind the vastness and unpredictability of the vocabulary asked in our exams. Welcome to our A2Z Vocabulary Booklet series!

1 First Reading: Start by reading only those words you’re already familiar with. Just skim through and highlight them with a marker. (Start with a singe letter first and then keep moving to the next) How to Use Your Vocabulary Booklet Effectively 2 Second Reading: Now revisit the words from the first reading. In this round, also include those words you’ve heard once or twice but don’t fully understand. Try to guess their meaning before checking it as this helps your brain engage. Start framing sentence by your own to hone your language skills & to easily recall the words 3 Third Reading: In this round, revise everything from the first & second readings. Then, focus on the words that are completely new to you, the ones you’ve never come across. These need the most attention, so spend more time understanding & using them.

Golden Rule: Don’t Get Overwhelmed The most important thing is don’t panic when you see too many words. Instead, fix a daily slot, even just 20– 30 minutes where you spend focused time with your vocabulary booklet. The key is to connect words with people around you like your friends, family members, or real-life situations. You can even make your own sentences to relate words better and remember them for long. This technique makes them easy to remember and much more fun to learn.

If you've neglected it or think of giving up too soon, this your wake-up call. It’s never too late. Start now, stay consistent, and trust the process. This booklet is enough! (provided you stay committed). And who knows? With regular practice, not only will you ace vocabulary questions in your exam… your friends might just start calling you the next Shashi Tharoor. 😉 All the best! As vocabulary is reduced , so are the number of feelings you can express, the number of events you can describe, the number of the things you can identify! Not only understanding is limited, but also experience. Man grows by language. Whenever he limits language he retrogresses!
